title: Fashion & Luxury
breadcrumb: Industries > Retail & Consumer Goods > Fashion & Luxury
meta_description: Fashion and luxury sell scarcity, story and service: assortment risk (the size-curve problem), authenticity, clienteling quality and channel consistency.

blocks.x: Fashion & Luxury: the operating units, priority programs and the five capability towers that matter most here.

The workflows we industrialize here: Assortment and buy planning, Boutique allocation, Clienteling and CRM, Authenticity services, Digital brand protection. Each arrives with its current cycle times measured in the Diagnose phase, and each leaves the program governed by outcome SLOs rather than anecdotes.

items: Assortment and buy decisions guess curves; end-of-season markdowns absorb the error.
Counterfeits and grey market erode brand equity; verification manual.
High-value client service depends on associate memory; digital channels generic.
Piece allocation to doors by rule of thumb; hero-SKU shortages.
Fake listings, phishing and counterfeit marketplaces unmonitored at scale.
Stores lack traffic/trial telemetry; experience investment unmeasured.

blocks.x: How we help — five priority capabilities

items: Curve modeling by door with demand transfer logic — sell-through up
Client history/preferences surfaced to associates: repeat spend up
Permissioned networks, tokenization and verifiable credentials with the reporting and controls supervisors expect.
Goal-directed agents that run inside your systems with defined roles, budgets and human checkpoints. Every action is logged, measurable and reversible.
Marketplace monitoring with takedown evidence: abuse scaled down

blocks.x: This sub-industry pattern gets a named pod: delivery lead, quality owner, control owner — running a follow-the-sun rhythm that covers build, run, and the conformance monitoring that keeps the design honest after handover.

items: Fresh waste down 28%, OOS down 31%: day-part demand and ordering agents
